extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators, teachers, and education researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical schema (Schoenfeld) characterizing the competencies required for mathematical problem solving, intended to guide instruction and assessment of learners' knowledge, strategies, metacognition, beliefs, and practices. Useful for designing curricula, classroom interventions, and teacher reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: The knowledge base
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundational domain knowledge that underpins problem solving (listed as 'I. The knowledge base').

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem solving strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of heuristics and strategies a solver can deploy (listed as 'II. Problem solving strategies').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: analogy, auxiliary elements, decomposing and recombining, induction, specialization, variation, working backwards (See Pólya).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and control (Metacognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing how and when to use resources and strategies effectively and efficiently (listed as 'III. Monitoring and control (Metacognition)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding metacognitive questions provided: 'What am I doing? Why am I doing it? How does it help me?' Emphasizes regulation of strategy selection and resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beliefs and affects
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners' beliefs about the nature of mathematics and emotional/attitudinal factors (listed as 'IV. Beliefs and affects').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical student beliefs enumerated (presented as problematic/characteristic): 'Mathematics problems have one and only one right answer.'; 'There is only one correct way to solve any mathematics problem -- usually the rule the teacher has most recently demonstrated to the class.'; 'Ordinary students cannot expect to understand mathematics; they expect simply to memorize it, and apply what they have learned mechanically and without understanding.'; 'Mathematics is a solitary activity, done by individuals in isolation.'; 'Students who have understood the mathematics they have studied will be able to solve any assigned problem in five minutes or less.'; 'The mathematics learned in school has little or nothing to do with the real world.'; 'Formal proof is irrelevant to processes of discovery or invention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The habits, dispositions, and social processes of interpretation and sense-making that constitute mathematical practice (listed as 'V. Practices').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that becoming a good problem solver involves acquiring habits and dispositions of interpretation and sense-making as much as skills and knowledge. Suggests conceiving of mathematics education as a socialization process rather than only instruction in specific skills (Resnick, 1989).
